chunks: And from him, from Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'In the case of a man who divorces his wife, he has the right to take her back (revise the divorce).' And he said: 'She is not given the final (third) divorce until he has had sexual intercourse with her.'

key_terms.يَمَسَّهَا: he touches her (referring to sexual intercourse)
key_terms.يُرَاجِعَ: to take back / revise (in the context of revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a revocable divorce and the final divorce in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the mechanics of *talaq raj'i* (revocable divorce), emphasizing that remarriage during the *iddah* requires no new contract, while also specifying that the finality of the third divorce is contingent upon actual consummation (*tamassus*), a key criterion in Shia fiqh for determining when the *khula'* or *mubara'ah* phase begins. The hadith underscores the importance of physical intimacy as the threshold for the irrevocability of the third divorce, distinguishing it from mere separation. This ruling is foundational in the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* for resolving disputes regarding the status of women in the intermediate stage of triple divorce.
